general_facts: 🦀 The Japanese spider crab has a leg span of up to 3.7 meters. The largest living arthropod. Worth knowing.
🦀 Horseshoe crabs are not true crabs. They're more closely related to spiders. This changes nothing about our work here.
🦀 The coconut crab can lift up to 28 kg. The strongest grip of any crustacean. Relevant to today's difficulty, arguably.
🦀 Crabs have been walking sideways for approximately 200 million years. If the approach works, don't fix it.
🦀 The yeti crab farms bacteria on its own claws for sustenance. Self-sufficient. Unlike some members of this colony.
🦀 A female blue crab mates only once but stores sperm for multiple clutches. Efficient resource management.
🦀 The decorator crab attaches sponges and algae to its shell for camouflage. Methodical. Strategic.
🦀 Fiddler crabs regenerate lost claws. The replacement is always smaller. Adaptation has costs.
🦀 The pea crab lives inside oysters and mussels. A controversial lifestyle choice, but effective.
🦀 Red king crabs can live up to 30 years in cold waters. Longevity rewards consistency.
🦀 Sally Lightfoot crabs can run in all four directions simultaneously. Versatile.
🦀 Crabs communicate through drumming and claw-waving. Complex signals. No vocalization needed.
🦀 The Dungeness crab fishery contributes approximately $220 million annually to the West Coast economy. The crabs receive none of it.
🦀 The porcelain crab has the fastest appendage movement in the animal kingdom. Faster than the mantis shrimp by acceleration.
🦀 The *Cardisoma guanhumi* can migrate up to 8 km from the ocean and still return. Impressive navigation.

new: 🌊 New moon. The tide swings to its spring maximum. *Uca* — the fiddler crabs — set their larval release to precisely this darkness. The colony keeps the schedule.
🦀 New moon. No light on the water, and the strongest tides of the month. The intertidal is at its most ambitious tonight.
waxing_crescent: 🦀 Waxing crescent. The tides begin to slacken from their peak. Foraging ranges are still generous. The specimens take advantage.
🌊 Waxing crescent. The moon returns to the sky by degrees. Many *Brachyura* are already reading the change in amplitude.
first_quarter: 🌊 First quarter. Neap tides — the water moves the least it will all month. Foraging ranges contract. The crabs conserve their effort.
🦀 First quarter moon. The tidal range is at its minimum. A quiet interval in the intertidal. The colony waits.
waxing_gibbous: 🦀 Waxing gibbous. The *Uca* population is aware. Activity climbs as the tides rebuild toward the full moon.
🌊 Waxing gibbous. The water reaches a little further up the shore each cycle now. Anticipation, if a tide can be said to anticipate.
full: 🌊 Full moon. Spring tides at their peak. *Gecarcinus* and *Uca* alike release their larvae into the strongest current of the month.
🦀 Full moon. Maximum tidal range, maximum light. Many crustaceans time their entire reproductive year to this single night.
waning_gibbous: 🦀 Waning gibbous. The tide's reach begins to recede. On Christmas Island, the *Gecarcoidea natalis* columns are, somewhere, already moving toward the sea.
🌊 Waning gibbous. The moon is past full and the spring tides ebb. The red crabs read the fading light.
last_quarter: 🌊 Last quarter. Neap tides return. The *Gecarcoidea natalis* spawning is timed to the turn of this exact high tide, before dawn — a precision that borders on the unreasonable.
🦀 Last quarter moon. The red crabs of Christmas Island release their eggs on the receding tide, now, and only now. The synchronisation is not a coincidence.
waning_crescent: 🦀 Waning crescent. The lunar cycle closes. The intertidal grows quiet, waiting for the new moon to restart a rhythm the crabs have kept for 200 million years.
🌊 Waning crescent. Almost no moon left. The tides are unremarkable. Even the crabs seem to be conserving material for the next cycle.
